title: Adaptive prefetch savings briefing (mar 23 2029)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, shareable bench + narrative for the adaptive prefetch prototype (v0.3) — focused on microburst / short-session workloads where prefetch amortization and KV-prefix warmness matter. Goal is to show realistic latency & dollars-per-1M-token impacts and a simple decision rubric for product/infra tradeoffs.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Adaptive prefetch (AP) reduces median latency by ~5-12% and p99 by 8-18% in microburst-dominated traces when prefetch hit-rate > 25%.
- Cost delta: ~-3% to -9% net token-cost for AP vs baseline when accounting for extra compute for prefetch work; larger savings at high KV reuse.
- Win conditions: sparse-session workloads with short turns (avg turn length < 40 tokens) and high re-use across turns. Not recommended as a default on long-turn streaming-heavy workloads.

Test matrix (short):
- Models: open-Llama-70b-quant (v1.2), redwood-chat-medium (hybrid-quant)
- HW: A100-80GB (single GPU), rtx-8000 equiv in edge-sim
- Workload shapes: microburst (bursts of 25 concurrent tiny sessions), steady chat (10k sustained qps), sparse sessions (long idle between turns)
- Configs: baseline (no prefetch), static prefetch (always prefetch next 64 toks), adaptive prefetch v0.3 (heuristic + short-window predictor)

Condensed numeric table (median / p90 / p99 latencies and cost-per-1M-tokens):

Scenario: microburst (avg turn 28 tokens)
| config           | median (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | $/1M tokens |
|------------------|-------------|----------|----------|-------------|
| baseline         | 120         | 240      | 690      | 112.4       |
| static-prefetch  | 110         | 210      | 630      | 118.6       |
| adaptive-prefetch| 102         | 195      | 565      | 105.7       |

Scenario: steady chat (avg turn 120 tokens)
| config           | median (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | $/1M tokens |
|------------------|-------------|----------|----------|-------------|
| baseline         | 220         | 410      | 980      | 96.2        |
| static-prefetch  | 225         | 420      | 1005     | 101.5       |
| adaptive-prefetch| 218         | 405      | 970      | 98.9        |

Interpretation notes on numbers above:
- Microburst: AP gives both latency and cost wins because prefetch work is targeted to sessions that will reuse KV state across rapid turns; static prefetch wastes cycles and increases token cost.
- Steady chat: limited headroom for AP; marginal latency pull-down but prefetch overhead sometimes increases cost slightly.

Percentile curves (ascii mini-chart, microburst, p99 focus):
- baseline p99: 690ms  |████████████████████████████████████████████████████|
- static-prefetch p99: 630ms |███████████████████████████████████████████████|
- adaptive-prefetch p99: 565ms |██████████████████████████████████████████|
(note: chart normalized to baseline width = 50 chars)

Key microbench observations (raw traces + flame-summaries):
- Prefetch hit-rate correlation: sessions with prefetch-hit >= 30% saw median drop ~15% and p99 ~22% vs baseline.
- Cold-prefix penalty: cold-start sessions where KV not yet populated saw AP add ~12-18ms overhead (prefetch wasted), but proportion of these sessions in our microburst trace is low (~11%).
- CPU offload: AP's heuristic controller requires a light CPU worker per GPU host; CPU usage rose +6% in our runs, negligible on typical infra but worth noting for edge t2-small hosts.

Cost accounting assumptions (how $/1M tokens computed):
- GPU time priced at internal cost (A100 slot) = $2.30/hr equivalent; amortized per-token using observed token/sec/runtime.
- Prefetch adds extra FLOPs which we convert to seconds-run on GPU; static prefetch pays this always, AP only when prediction > threshold.
- Networking and memory egress ignored (same across configs).
- These are platform-internal economics for decision-making, not external MSRP.

Sensitivity grid (high-level):
- When prefetch hit-rate < 10%: AP and static both increase cost; baseline preferred.
- Hit-rate 10-25%: AP slightly positive on p50 but cost-neutral; consider canary.
- Hit-rate >25%: AP tends to be both lower latency and lower cost vs baseline (best-case).

Operator checklist for canary rollout (recommended incremental path):
1) Canary AP on 5% of microburst-like traffic only (route by session-length heuristic).
2) Monitor p50/p90/p99, KV hit-rate, CPU host utilization; create alert if p99 increases by >5% for >10 minutes.
3) If token-cost per 1M tokens improves >2% and p99 improves >8% after 24h, expand to 25%.
4) Run negative control (static prefetch) alongside to validate predictions.

Action items (short-term):
- [ ] Expose prefetch confidence metric in tracing (Jon) — INF-1345
- [ ] Add cost breakdown to console per-route (Marta) — dashboard stub in confluence/INF-9273
- [ ] Run edge-sim on RTX class host profile and capture CPU tradeoffs (Samir)

Open questions / unknowns:
- How does AP interact with multi-tenant slot packing when prefetch work triggers host-level contention? quick sim pending.
- Prediction model: current v0.3 uses heuristic window; we should evaluate a small learned predictor (lightweight logistic) next quarter.
- Security: prefetch loads user KV hints; ensure no additional data-surface for multi-tenant leakage — security review recommended.

Notes to self / rough TODO for followups:
- Add a compact waterfall plot for per-request component times (KV fetch, compute, prefetch overlap).
- Run ablation that toggles prefetch-size (32/64/128) and predictor-threshold grid in a single sweep.
- Draft a one-pager for product that states when to toggle AP per customer SLA tier.

Appendix A: short methodology (how we measured)
- Synthetic replay of production traces (sampled microburst cohort, anonymized), replayed at 1x and 5x pressure.
- Each run: 3 warmup minutes, 20 minute measurement window. Reported values are median across 5 independent runs.
- Instrumentation: internal tracing hooks for prefetch events, KV hit/miss tagged, and host-level CPU/GPU counters.

Appendix B: sample log snippet (representative microburst session)
[2029-03-21T14:12:03Z] session=abc123 turn=1 recv=18 tokens -> prefetch:predict=0.72 -> spawn-prefetch(size=64)
[2029-03-21T14:12:03Z] session=abc123 turn=2 recv=12 tokens -> prefetch:hit=true kv-hitrate=0.83 latency=95ms

If this looks useful I can convert the tables to small charts for the product one-pager and add the raw CSVs to the linked JIRA. Feedback: want more long-tail exploration (p999) or edge-host profiles next?

-- Aisha
